originality.rationale: The 2021 full primary article supplies Esakia duality and finite Boolean cascades but not this explicit prefix/tail normal form or its complete hom-set, image-rank and idempotent formulas in the inspected sections. Semantic searches in the indexed mathematical record located ordinary monotone-map enumeration and ordinary retraction theorems, which do not imply counts under the strictly stronger bounded-morphism condition. No equivalent specialized result was found. Older general Heyting endomorphism literature is incompletely accessible, creating a named residual risk rather than a claim of proven uniqueness.
residual_risks: Older general Heyting endomorphism literature (including Pultr–Sichler 1997 and Adams–Koubek–Sichler 1985) was not inspected at full-text depth; a special case could be present.
Indexed weak-order mapping-space and retraction records were available only by abstracts/summaries; those snippets do not establish whole-document noncoverage.
Alternative formulations via correct E-partitions and transformation-semigroup structural theory may encode the same formula without using p-morphism terminology.
Search evidence supports a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a mathematical proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: A natural semantic compatibility problem for finite weak-Pierce Kripke frames and their dual Boolean-cascade Heyting algebras is solved completely within the nondegenerate class: exact all-height hom-set census, image-rank generating polynomial and idempotent/retraction counts. The boundary a_i,b_i>=2 is essential; singleton levels admit mixed-level behavior. These are structural invariants of all finite sizes and genuinely stronger than sample table values.
